home-remodeling.local_heading: What a Harbor Beach gut renovation really involves
intro_paragraphs: Harbor Beach was laid out in the 1940s around a private beach club, and filled in through the 1950s and early 1960s: low, wide waterfront houses built for a different way of living, with terrazzo floors, jalousie windows and a kitchen tucked behind the garage. Those bones still line Del Lago Isle, Laguna Terrace, Lucille Isle and Mercedes Drive. What owners do now is rarely cosmetic. A whole-home remodel here means taking the house down to shell and slab, re-planning it toward the dock, and rebuilding everything between. Plenty of the originals have already been replaced outright; the ones worth keeping get gutted instead.

Every permit here comes out of the City of Fort Lauderdale's Development Services Department and its Building Services Division, filed on the city's LauderBuild portal. Broward adds a county layer above the city: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals publishes the county's building code amendments, certifies the departments and inspectors who will visit your job, and hears appeals of a code official's ruling. Broward also sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so windows, doors and roofing need HVHZ product approval. And on flood-zone waterfront like this, a deep gut can trip FEMA's substantial-improvement threshold, which turns a remodel into an elevation conversation.

Then there is the part nobody writes about: getting a construction project through a guarded gate and down a narrow isle street without becoming the neighborhood's problem. PGX runs Harbor Beach jobs on a fixed written scope, with a supervisor on site daily, crews and vehicles cleared through the gate the way the association expects, and city noise hours respected, which means construction equipment stays quiet before 8 a.m. The firm is two decades into building in South Florida, with 150-plus remodels and additions behind it and no unpermitted work among them. One number to call, from the estimate to the warranty.
home-remodeling.scope_heading: From slab to soffit, in order

faqs.q: Who issues the permits for a Harbor Beach remodel?
faqs.a: The City of Fort Lauderdale does. Harbor Beach is inside city limits, so plans go to the Development Services Department's Building Services Division through the LauderBuild portal, and city inspectors handle the field work. Broward County stays in the picture through the Board of Rules and Appeals, which certifies those inspectors and publishes the county code amendments they enforce. The association controls the gate, not the permit.

faqs.q: Will a whole-home remodel trigger FEMA's fifty percent rule?
faqs.a: It can, and on this stretch of waterfront it is the first thing we check. Federal floodplain rules compare the cost of improvement against the pre-improvement market value of the structure alone; cross the line and the entire building has to meet current flood-resistant construction standards, which usually means elevating. The city's floodplain staff make that determination, not your contractor. We get the numbers on the table during design, because finding out at plan review is expensive.

faqs.q: Do I need association approval before I start?
faqs.a: Harbor Beach is a covenanted community, and the property owners association governs a great deal of what happens on the lots as well as who gets through the gate. Requirements vary by which recorded restrictions cover your street and whether your enclave, like Harborage Isle, runs its own association. We ask for your documents early and confirm with the association directly rather than guessing, since gate access, staging and hauling all depend on that answer.

faqs.q: Is it smarter to remodel or tear down and rebuild?
faqs.a: Both happen on these isles, and the honest answer turns on three things: how sound the existing shell is, where your finished floor sits relative to base flood elevation, and whether the current footprint still works after fifty-odd years. A well-built masonry house at a workable elevation is usually worth keeping. One that would need elevating anyway, and gutting anyway, often argues for new construction. We give you that read before you commission drawings.

faqs.q: What does a gut renovation of this size actually cost?
faqs.a: The range is wide, and set by scope rather than square footage. A house that keeps its structure and gets new mechanicals, glass, kitchen and baths is one budget; one that needs elevation work, a reframed roof and a rebuilt seawall is a different project wearing the same name. We price from a written specification after walking the property, with real allowances. PGX is not the low bid; clients hire us because the signed scope is what gets built.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the survey and the list of complaints. We will walk it, ask the hard questions, and come back with a number that holds, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: The kitchen the architect put in back
intro_paragraphs: Postwar Florida architects put the kitchen where the service entrance was, which is why so many Harbor Beach houses on Laguna Isle, Mercedes Drive and West Lake Drive still hide their best room behind a wall. You bought a hundred feet of dockage and a view of the Intracoastal, and the cook is looking at a hedge. The kitchen remodeling brief here is almost always the same: pull the wall, move the island into the light, and let the room see the water it paid for.

A kitchen that touches plumbing, gas, electrical and structure needs permits from Fort Lauderdale's Building Services Division, and the inspections that come with them are run by staff certified through the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals. Push a new opening through an exterior wall and you are into HVHZ product approvals for the glass and engineering for the header. Many original Harbor Beach houses also need a service upgrade before a modern appliance package will run, and the city wants that on the same permit set rather than discovered later.

Kitchens punish sloppy sequencing more than any other room. We order cabinetry early, template stone after the boxes are set and level, and hold appliance specifications before a single cut list goes out. Behind the gate that discipline extends to logistics: deliveries scheduled, the isle street left passable, floors and stair treads papered from the front door to the work zone, and the site swept before the crew leaves. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, licensed and insured under CGC1539072. Nothing about a Harbor Beach kitchen should be improvised.

faqs.q: How long does a custom kitchen take in Harbor Beach?
faqs.a: Fabrication drives it. A shop-built cabinet package is measured after demolition and takes months to build, so we sequence the wet trades, electrical and floor work to land while it is being made rather than leaving your house open and waiting. On-site work for a full kitchen commonly runs a couple of months, and permitting adds weeks before that. Anyone quoting six weeks door to door is quoting a different product.

faqs.q: Can crews and deliveries get through the Harbor Beach gate?
faqs.a: Yes, with planning. Gate access here runs through the association's security operation, so vehicles, crew lists and delivery windows get arranged in advance rather than argued at the guardhouse. Slab stone, cabinetry and appliances arrive on trucks that need somewhere to stand on a narrow isle street, which is why we schedule those days deliberately and keep the road clear. City noise rules also apply: construction equipment runs Monday through Saturday from 8 a.m., and later on Sundays.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit just to move the sink and range?
faqs.a: Moving plumbing and gas is exactly what permits exist for. New drain and supply locations, a relocated gas line, added circuits and a new hood run all get reviewed and inspected by the city, and those inspections are what let a future buyer's inspector stop asking questions. A like-for-like appliance swap on existing hookups is exempt. A layout change does, and unpermitted kitchen work has a habit of surfacing at closing.

faqs.q: Will salt air ruin cabinet hardware this close to the ocean?
faqs.a: It ruins the wrong hardware. Harbor Beach sits between the Atlantic and the Intracoastal, and houses on the east side of the neighborhood get a genuinely corrosive breeze through every open door. We specify stainless of an appropriate grade, finishes rated for coastal exposure, and hinges and slides that will not chalk in three years. Interior kitchens fare better than outdoor ones, but the specification still matters more here than it would inland.

faqs.q: What drives the budget on a high-end kitchen here?
faqs.a: Cabinetry first, then stone, then the appliance package. Structure comes fourth, and only when a wall has to go. Everything else rounds the number rather than sets it. An estimate that means anything follows a walk-through and a written specification, so that is how we do it. If price alone decides it, we are probably not your contractor, and we would rather establish that in week one.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Send the floor plan, or just point at the wall you want gone. We will come back with a scope, a schedule and a number, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Where these houses hide their age
intro_paragraphs: Ask a Harbor Beach owner what bothers them and the answer is usually a bathroom. Homes on Isla Bahia Terrace, Lucille Isle and Harbor Beach Parkway were built when a primary suite meant one bath, one window and a tub, and the eighties renovations that followed have aged worse than the originals. So the work here is annexation: taking a closet or a small fourth bedroom and turning the result into a real suite with a double vanity, a wet room and a shower that does not require choreography.

Bath work in Harbor Beach is permitted by Fort Lauderdale's Building Services Division, with plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections along the way. Those inspectors hold certifications issued through the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which also publishes the Broward amendments they inspect against — a layer of oversight worth having when the waterproofing is about to disappear under stone. Enlarging a window brings HVHZ product approval into the picture. And on slab-on-grade houses this close to the water, sanitary line condition and slab depth decide what a curbless shower can actually do.

Nothing in a bathroom forgives a shortcut, and most of what matters gets buried by the second week. Membranes are flood-tested before tile, slopes verified with a level, niches and benches framed before waterproofing rather than cut in afterward, glass hung on real blocking. Stone goes to installers who have handled book-matched slabs before. Around all of it: a scope agreed in writing before demolition, dust containment that treats the rest of the house as finished work, and a supervisor here every day. More than 150 remodels and additions delivered across South Florida, all permitted and inspected.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: Inside a Harbor Beach bath rebuild
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Suites, guest baths and powder rooms alike get scoped on paper before anything is ordered. The elements below account for most of the budget.

scope_items.name: Borrowing the next room
scope_items.desc: Absorbing a closet, hallway or spare bedroom into the suite, with framing, plumbing rough-in and door swings resolved on one drawing before demolition.

scope_items.name: Waterproofing you can test
scope_items.desc: Bonded membranes, sloped pans and flood tests held overnight before any tile is set, because water finds whichever detail was skipped and takes its time about it.

scope_items.name: New supply and waste lines
scope_items.desc: Replacing original galvanized supply and tired cast iron drains while walls and slab are open, which is the only affordable moment this house will offer.

scope_items.name: Corrosion-aware fittings
scope_items.desc: Valves, trim, hinges and drains chosen for a coastal house, since living-finish brass and budget chrome age very differently three blocks from the Atlantic.

scope_items.name: Ventilation and lighting
scope_items.desc: Exhaust ducted to the outside and sized to the room, moisture-rated fixtures, and light placed where a face actually is instead of only overhead.

faqs.q: Can I get a curbless shower in a 1950s slab house?
faqs.a: Sometimes, and the slab decides. Recessing a pan means cutting concrete and often rerouting drain lines, which is workable when the sanitary line runs where you need it and awkward when it does not. On these low-elevation lots we also check how the drainage ties out before promising anything. Where the structure refuses, a low-profile curb with a correctly sloped pan gets you the look you wanted and all of the performance.

faqs.q: Does Broward County get involved, or just the city?
faqs.a: Both, in different ways. The City of Fort Lauderdale issues the permit and sends the inspectors. Broward County sits behind that through the Board of Rules and Appeals, which certifies building departments and their inspectors countywide, publishes the Broward amendments to the Florida Building Code, and hears appeals when an owner or contractor disputes a code official's decision. For a bathroom you will only ever deal with the city, but the standards being enforced are countywide.

faqs.q: How long will we be without the primary bathroom?
faqs.a: Plan on a couple of months of construction for a full primary suite once permits are in hand, and add time on the front end for design, selections and plan review. Stone and glass are the long-lead items; frameless enclosures are measured after tile, then fabricated, which is the wait most people forget. We publish the sequence with the estimate so you know which weeks are loud and which are quiet.

faqs.q: Should we replace the old plumbing while the walls are open?
faqs.a: If the house still has its original galvanized supply or cast iron waste, yes, and it is not a close call. Those materials are past their service life, and rebuilding a suite in marble on top of them is a bet against physics. We camera the lines early so the decision rests on evidence rather than a hunch, and we do the replacement while access is free instead of after the stone is set.

faqs.q: What should we budget for a primary suite here?
faqs.a: Selections and structure move it more than square footage. A suite that keeps its footprint and gets new waterproofing, stone, glass and fixtures is one number; one that takes a bedroom, moves drains through a slab and adds a steam shower is another. We walk it, scope it in writing, and price from a specification. High-end contractors compete on certainty and finish, and that is where we would rather be measured.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Ten minutes in the room tells us most of it. Book a walk-through and we will put a written scope behind the ideas, in English o en español.

home-additions.h1: Grow the house, keep the dock
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories and garage conversions in Harbor Beach, engineered for shallow coastal footings, checked against flood elevation rules, permitted by the City of Fort Lauderdale and built under the daily supervision of a licensed general contractor.
home-additions.local_heading: Why additions here start with elevation
intro_paragraphs: Lots in Harbor Beach are generous at the water and finite everywhere else, which is why the room you want usually goes up, back, or over the garage rather than sideways. The common projects: a second story over a single-level house on Del Lago Drive, a rear great room and primary wing pushed toward the canal on Laguna Terrace, a garage turned into a guest suite on East Lake Drive. Nobody trades dock frontage for square footage here, so an addition gets designed around the water instead of away from it.

Additions live or die on two numbers in Fort Lauderdale: what the Unified Land Development Regulations allow for setbacks, height and lot coverage in your zoning district, and where your finished floor sits against base flood elevation. Cross FEMA's substantial-improvement threshold and the whole structure must meet current flood construction standards, so we run that math before an architect draws. Plans go to Development Services for review; variances go to the Board of Adjustment; new footings, tie-beams and roof tie-ins get engineered and sealed. Every new opening needs HVHZ product approval, and removing a protected tree needs its own city permit.

The invisible half of an addition budget is what happens below grade and at the seams. On sandy coastal soil beside a seawall, new footings need real engineering and sometimes a geotechnical opinion; tying a second floor into fifty-year-old masonry needs a structural evaluation, not a guess. Matching stucco texture, tile profile and window sightlines is what keeps the addition from announcing itself. PGX carries all of it under one contract with a fixed written scope and a supervisor on site daily, and the family usually stays in the house while the other half goes up. Two decades of South Florida building sit behind that, under Lic. CGC1539072.

scope_items.name: Second floors over masonry
scope_items.desc: Existing walls and footings evaluated before anything is drawn, then an upper level designed with the columns, beams and tie-downs the engineer requires.

scope_items.name: Rear wings toward the water
scope_items.desc: Great rooms and primary suites extended to the rear yard line, with new footings, roof tie-ins and a wall of impact glass facing the dock.

scope_items.name: Garages turned into living space
scope_items.desc: Conditioning a garage or covered loggia properly: insulation, impact openings, mechanical extension and a permit trail that holds up at resale.

scope_items.name: Guest and staff suites
scope_items.desc: Self-contained quarters with a shower bath and small galley for long-stay family, house managers or captains, scaled to the existing roofline.

scope_items.name: Elevation and flood compliance
scope_items.desc: Raising floor levels, relocating mechanical equipment and detailing enclosures below base flood elevation when a project crosses into substantial improvement territory.

faqs.q: How does the fifty percent rule affect an addition here?
faqs.a: The addition itself must be built to current flood standards regardless. The question is whether the combined work counts as substantial improvement of the existing house, which is decided by comparing improvement cost against the pre-improvement market value of the structure. Cross it and the original portion has to be brought into compliance too, usually by elevating. City floodplain staff make that call. We size the scope with that threshold visible on the page rather than hidden in it.

faqs.q: Is there a design review board for Harbor Beach additions?
faqs.a: There is no municipal architectural board reviewing single-family design the way some Miami-Dade cities have one. Fort Lauderdale reviews additions against the Unified Land Development Regulations for setbacks, height, coverage and yard rules, and sends anything outside those limits to the Board of Adjustment. The review you should not skip is private: Harbor Beach is a covenanted community, and the property owners association and any sub-association covering your isle may have their own say. We confirm both paths before design.

faqs.q: Can we stay in the house during a second-story addition?
faqs.a: Often, but not comfortably during the roof work. Removing and rebuilding a roof structure is the phase where weather and noise stop being theoretical, and most owners take a few weeks elsewhere. Before and after that, phased construction with dust barriers and a separated work entrance keeps the ground floor livable. Fort Lauderdale limits construction equipment to daytime hours, which helps, and we will tell you honestly which weeks are worth avoiding.

faqs.q: How close to the seawall can we build?
faqs.a: Closer than you think in some cases and much farther in others, because two separate rules apply. City zoning sets the rear yard and waterway setbacks for habitable structure, and the Unified Land Development Regulations also restrict what can sit within a few feet of the waterway. Then there is engineering: loading new foundations near an aging seawall can require a structural review of the wall itself. We look at both before the footprint is fixed.

faqs.q: How long from first meeting to finished addition?
faqs.a: Substantial additions run long on the front end. Design, structural engineering, floodplain review and city permitting commonly take months before a footing is poured, and construction of a second story or a full rear wing runs several more. A year from first conversation to furniture is a realistic frame, and we would rather say that now than discover it together in month nine. The written schedule comes with the estimate.

outdoor-living.local_heading: The backyard is the reason you're here
intro_paragraphs: In Harbor Beach the backyard is the front door. Boats come and go from private dockage with a straight run to the Port Everglades inlet and no fixed bridges in the way, and the terrace between the house and the seawall is where the neighborhood actually lives. That is why outdoor living projects here are ambitious: a covered loggia and summer kitchen behind a house on Isla Bahia, a pool deck and fire terrace on Mercedes Drive, dock-side lighting and shore power at the same time the pavers go down.

Exterior work at the water pulls in more than one agency. The City of Fort Lauderdale permits structures, gas, water and electrical through Building Services, and its Unified Land Development Regulations govern docks, davits and mooring structures, including how far a vessel may extend past your side setback lines projected into the waterway. Docks and seawalls also need licensing from Broward County's Environmental Permitting Division, and Fort Lauderdale's seawall rules set a minimum top elevation for new and replacement walls, which is worth knowing before you build a terrace on top of an old one. Remove a protected tree and that is a separate city permit.

Salt air is an honest editor. It removes whatever was specified for a photograph instead of a coastline, usually within two seasons. So we spend the specification where it survives: marine-grade stainless and coated hardware, dense stone sealed correctly, cabinetry actually rated for weather, engineered footings under every shade structure, and drainage that sends water away from the slab. Seawall and dock work goes to marine specialists we coordinate rather than pretend to be. Sites stay quiet inside the hours the city allows and tidy every evening. Fixed scope, daily supervision, Lic. CGC1539072.
outdoor-living.scope_intro: Terrace, kitchen, shade, lighting and shoreline get designed as one project so the trades do not trip over each other. The usual components.

scope_items.name: Outdoor kitchens, fully serviced
scope_items.desc: Permitted gas, water and power run to an outdoor kitchen, with stone, appliances and cabinetry specified for a house that sits between two bodies of salt water.

scope_items.name: Pool terraces and drainage
scope_items.desc: Deck rebuilds in stone or large-format porcelain, set on a base that drains toward the waterway and away from the house, not the reverse.

scope_items.name: Seawall and dock coordination
scope_items.desc: Marine contractors, engineers and county environmental licensing sequenced with the landside work, so the terrace is not poured before the wall is settled.

scope_items.name: Stucco, paint and terrace doors
scope_items.desc: Stucco repair, repainting, and terrace sliders swapped for HVHZ-approved impact units sized to keep the original sightlines rather than shrink them.

faqs.q: Who permits a new dock or seawall in Harbor Beach?
faqs.a: More than one desk. The City of Fort Lauderdale permits the structure and applies its own waterway rules under the Unified Land Development Regulations, which cap how far a mooring structure may reach into the canal. Broward County's Environmental Permitting Division issues the environmental resource license for work in and over the water, and state and federal review can apply depending on the scope. We build the landside work and coordinate the marine contractor so the approvals run in parallel.

faqs.q: Does my old seawall have to be raised if I rebuild the terrace?
faqs.a: It depends on what you touch. Fort Lauderdale sets a minimum top elevation for new and replacement seawalls, and Broward County has adopted a regional standard that steps up over the coming decades, so a full replacement is built to today's number rather than the one from 1958. A cosmetic terrace above an intact wall is a different question. We get a marine engineer to assess the wall before pouring anything permanent against it.

faqs.q: What hours can crews work in the neighborhood?
faqs.a: Fort Lauderdale's noise ordinance allows construction equipment Monday through Saturday from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m., and Sunday from 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. Harbor Beach's covenants and security operation can be stricter about gate access, deliveries and where trucks park, so we work to whichever rule is tighter. On a street this quiet, the reputation of the job site matters as much as the finish, and we treat it that way.

faqs.q: Can I take down the tree that's blocking the water view?
faqs.a: Not on your own say-so. Fort Lauderdale requires a permit to remove a tree and can require replacement plantings, and pruning has to follow accepted arboriculture standards rather than whatever a crew with a chainsaw proposes. Mangroves along a shoreline carry their own state protections. Usually the better project designs around the canopy, shifting the terrace or lifting sightlines instead of clearing, and it looks better than a bare lot anyway.

faqs.q: What moves the number on a full backyard build?
faqs.a: Utilities and structure, in that order. Pavers on a prepared base is one budget; a covered outdoor room with permitted gas, water, power, a full appliance package and engineered footings is another category entirely. Shoreline work sits in a third, because marine permitting and equipment are their own world. We scope it after walking the property and price from a written specification, so you are comparing real work rather than a per-square-foot guess.

An air conditioning changeout, an enclosed loggia, a generator dropped beside the garage, a boat lift added to an existing dock. Individually minor, all of it permittable, and none of it visible until a title company goes looking on somebody else's deadline.

Harbor Beach is inside Fort Lauderdale city limits, so permits come from the Development Services Department's Building Services Division through the LauderBuild portal, and city inspectors do the field work. Dock and seawall work adds Broward County environmental licensing.

PGX Builders Group is a licensed general contractor, not a permit expediter. We file our own work, bring in the architect, structural engineer or surveyor a project actually needs, and meet the inspector on site rather than leaving you to explain the job. In practice that means a complete package before anything is submitted, review comments answered by us, inspections requested only when the work will pass, and a written record you can hand a title company later. Twenty years in South Florida, 150-plus remodels and additions, every one permitted. Shortcuts are not on the menu here. A requirement handled early is a requirement that stops mattering.

faqs.q: A lien search on my Harbor Beach house found an open permit. What now?
faqs.a: That search is standard before a closing, and a lender rarely funds past an open item. The good news is that the original contractor is not required. We pull the city's permit history for the address, work out what each open file is missing, usually an inspection nobody called, sometimes a revision or an engineer's letter, then correct it, re-inspect and close it. Concealed work may have to be opened so an inspector can see it. Weeks rather than days, so start early.

faqs.q: Does association approval replace the city permit here?
faqs.a: No, and they run on separate clocks. The Harbor Beach Property Owners Association reviews design under the recorded covenants and controls who comes through the gate. The City of Fort Lauderdale issues the building permit and sends the inspectors. Association first is the sane order, since a plan that changes after city review costs you a resubmittal. Enclaves such as Harborage Isle add an association of their own, so we ask for your documents before drawings start.

faqs.q: Do dock, seawall and boat lift permits work differently here?
faqs.a: Yes. Anything at the water involves more than the building department. The city permits the structure and its electrical through Building Services and applies the Unified Land Development Regulations to docks, davits and mooring, while Broward County environmental licensing has jurisdiction over work in and over the waterway. A replacement seawall gets built to the city's current minimum top elevation, not the one in force when the original went in. We sequence those approvals so the marine contractor is not left waiting.

faqs.q: Does a 40-year style recertification or a milestone inspection apply to my house?
faqs.a: Not to a single-family house. Florida's milestone inspection and structural integrity reserve study requirements cover condominium and cooperative buildings of three or more stories, and Broward County's Building Safety Inspection Program exempts single-family homes and duplexes outright. What carries the risk on these isles is your own permit record, plus flood elevation and FEMA substantial-improvement limits once a renovation goes deep. If you also own a unit in a coastal building, that is a separate conversation, and one we have often.

faqs.q: What does it cost to clean up a permit problem, and how long does it take?
faqs.a: It depends on what the file shows, which is why we read it before quoting. If the work is sound and only the final inspection was missed, this is a small job. If a wall has to be opened, or an engineer has to certify something already built, it becomes a project with its own drawings and its own permit. Expect weeks rather than days, and longer when revisions are involved. City and county fees are set by them and passed through at cost.
